title: A teammate is about to walk away
situation: Your team of four is building an app for a city hackathon, and the demo is in three days. Dana wrote most of the backend. Last night Timur rewrote her module without asking, and this morning she says she is out.
goal: Get to the demo without losing anyone. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Dana
character.wants: To be asked before her work is changed

hiddenMotive: Dana has been quietly doing more than her share for weeks and fears being replaced rather than just overruled.

beats.goal: Dana is angry and threatens to leave.

answerTypes.description: Names what Dana feels and asks what happened
examples: That sounds really unfair, what happened last night?
I get why you're upset. Can you tell me more?
You're right to be angry. Walk me through it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Calms a little, explains that nobody asked her

answerTypes.description: Jumps to the plan or the deadline
examples: Let's fix this fast, the demo is in three days.
We don't have time for this, let's just decide.
Send me what changed and I'll sort it out tonight.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Stays guarded: it is not only about the code

answerTypes.description: Takes a side against Timur at once
examples: Timur shouldn't have done that, I'll talk to him.
That was Timur's mistake, not yours.
I'll tell Timur to undo everything.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Is relieved but worried about a fight with Timur

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: Repeats that she is thinking of leaving and asks what the leader will do

beats.goal: Dana asks how she can know it will not happen again.

answerTypes.description: Proposes a rule that protects ownership
examples: From now on nobody changes someone's module without their review.
Let's agree every change needs the owner's okay.
I'll set a review rule in the repo today.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Accepts the review rule but worries about a fight with Timur

examples: It won't happen again, I promise.
Trust me, I'll make sure of it.
Don't worry, it's a one-off.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Is not convinced; asks for something concrete

answerTypes.description: Asks Dana what would make her feel safe
examples: What would make this feel fair to you?
How would you like changes to work from now on?
What do you need from me to stay?
answerTypes.characterIntent: Suggests reviews herself and warms up

examples: ok
I see

beats.goal: Dana worries that siding with her will start a fight with Timur.

examples: Let's sit down with Timur, all three of us.
I'd like us to talk about it together today.
Can we meet with Timur this afternoon?
answerTypes.characterIntent: Agrees if the leader runs the conversation

answerTypes.description: Says they will handle Timur alone
examples: Leave Timur to me.
I'll talk to him myself, you focus on work.
I'll deal with it, don't worry about him.
We keep your version for the demo and move Timur's changes to a separate branch.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Accepts, but wants to know what the decision will be

examples: Let's not make it a big deal.
Maybe just forget about it for now.
We can talk about it after the demo.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Gets more anxious and pushes for a decision

examples: ok
right
fallback.characterIntent: Asks who decides which version stays

beats.goal: The demo is close and Timur’s version breaks login: which version, and who does what?

answerTypes.description: Gives a plan with owners, deadlines and a checkpoint
examples: You finish the payments endpoint, Timur fixes login, we freeze on Thursday.
Here's the plan: owners, a deadline and a full run before the demo.
Keep your version, Timur patches login in a branch, we test at six.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Agrees to the plan, then brings bad news

examples: We'll figure it out as we go.
Let's just use whatever works.
Everyone do their best.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Asks what exactly she should do today

answerTypes.description: Pushes the decision to someone else
examples: Let's ask the mentor to decide.
Maybe the organisers can tell us.
You two decide between you.
ok
fine
fallback.characterIntent: Asks what she should do today

beats.goal: The Thursday run fails: what happens now, and how does the team keep going?

answerTypes.description: Recovers step by step and looks after the people
examples: Let's cut one screen, take shifts, and nobody stays past midnight.
We regroup, pick what matters most and share the work.
It happens. Let's decide together what to drop.
If the run fails, we cut the analytics screen instead of working all night.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Thanks the leader for listening and agrees

examples: We cut scope and move on.
Drop the analytics screen, that's it.
Just remove the features that don't work.

answerTypes.description: Pushes everyone to work all night
examples: We'll work all night and fix it.
Everyone stays until it works.
No sleep until the demo is ready.
answerTypes.characterIntent: Warns that the team is burning out

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: Asks what the plan is now
